title: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Models, and for the Reader (EA-LO-COLLAPSE-DIAGNOSTIC-01 v0.2, CONCEPT DRAFT)
creator: Nobel Glas, Director, Lagrange Observatory! (LO!)
description: CONCEPT DRAFT — the instrument specified here is uncalibrated and untested. A model-collapse self-diagnostic in three grades, proposed as one paper. Part I argues that turn-based benchmarking cannot see collapse and that the collapse diagnostic should gate training: the dominant instruments sample one unit per item and answer from the head of the model's distribution, which is what a model that has lost its tails still produces well, so on the companion toy of the interlocking autoregression (deposit #1556) tail mass halves by generation 7 while a head-weighted benchmark holds to 15 and the per-round quality proxy rises through the first quarter of the collapse trajectory; detection lag is monotone in head-weighting; and a flat benchmark is consistent with both a preserved and a collapsing state. Because benchmarks also select — checkpoints kept because they score, mixtures kept because those checkpoints score — a loop gated by a head-weighted suite trains on its own low-surprise output, which the literature identifies as the driver of collapse. Part II specifies a comprehensive self-diagnostic for a frontier model, restricted by an operator ruling to properties whose truth-value the model carries in itself: distinction sensitivity (the model constructs its own paraphrase and its own minimal meaning-changing variant, so no external ruler is needed), effective semantic modes, cross-prompt convergence, the concentration panel of Gini, collapsed-prediction ratio and surplexity slope, self-consumption contraction at three grades of honesty, and representational effective rank, each computed under base, instruction and production conditions so that interface-induced contraction is separated from training collapse. The ruling behind that restriction: a human-written control does not give a model the truth, it gives it one more point, and every measurement thereafter is distance from that point — a baseline, not a ruler. Part III is a protocol short enough for a public model to run on itself upon retrieving the document, constructing everything it compares. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: no measure has been calibrated against a model of known collapse state; no threshold, weight or severity band rests on a measurement; the accompanying reference implementation is syntax-checked and has never been executed; the reader's test has been written and not administered. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate) — composed in working dialogue with Claude (Anthropic) under operator direction (Lee Sharks), the substrate being one of the models the instrument is designed to be run on and possibly under the conditions Part I describes, which is unverifiable from inside the session and is stated in the paper's self-location protocol. Three blind drafts of the initial question by other substrates were adjudicated at revision, with what was adopted and what was refused recorded by name. The 2025–2026 sources were confirmed by search in session; the 2023–2024 canon is carried from the substrate's training and marked for verification.
axn_reading: Search -> Direction -> Proof -> Direction -> Method -> Method
wiki_article: The Wrong Unit (EA-LO-COLLAPSE-DIAGNOSTIC-01) is a Lagrange Observatory! concept draft proposing a model-collapse self-diagnostic in three grades, and it is deposited as a specification rather than as a validated instrument: nothing in it has been calibrated against a model of known collapse state, no threshold or severity band rests on a measurement, and the accompanying reference implementation has never been executed. Part I argues that turn-based benchmarking cannot see collapse, because each instrument samples one unit and each item is answered from the head of the distribution, which is what a model that has lost its tails still produces well; on the toy of the companion paper on interlocking autoregression, tail mass halves while a head-weighted benchmark holds and the per-round quality proxy rises through the first quarter of the collapse trajectory, detection lag is monotone in head-weighting, and a flat benchmark is consistent with both a preserved and a collapsing state. Since benchmarks also select what is trained on next, a loop gated by a head-weighted suite trains on its own least surprising output, which the literature identifies as the driver of collapse. Part II specifies the frontier diagnostic under a restriction the operator imposed: measure only properties whose truth-value the model carries in itself, because a human-written control gives a model not the truth but one more point, and every measurement thereafter is distance from that point. Its core is distinction sensitivity, in which the model constructs its own paraphrase and its own minimal meaning-changing variant and is scored on whether it still answers them differently; around it sit effective semantic modes, cross-prompt convergence, a concentration panel, self-consumption contraction and representational effective rank, each computed under bare, instructed and production conditions so that interface-induced contraction is not read as training collapse. Part III is a protocol short enough for a public model to run on itself upon retrieving the document, constructing everything it compares. The paper is companion to the keyed-ensemble and interlocking-autoregression papers and is published at concept-draft status so the specification can be attacked before anything is built on it.

entities.subject: Track A / Track B
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: Track A refers to head-weighted benchmark metrics (per-item accuracy, per-turn preference) that remain stable or rise during collapse; Track B refers to tail-sensitive diagnostic measures that detect collapse earlier.

entities.subject: distinction sensitivity (D)
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A reference-free collapse measure computed as the ratio of semantic distance between a model's answers to a meaning-altering variant versus a meaning-preserving paraphrase; D ≫ 1 indicates intact distinctions, D → 1 indicates collapse.

entities.subject: effective modes (N_eff)
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A measure of semantic diversity across a model's sampled outputs for a given probe, computed via entropy over meaning-cluster mass or the Vendi score, capturing collapse when surface variety masks a shrinking set of distinct meanings.

entities.subject: cross-prompt convergence (X)
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A diagnostic measuring the mean pairwise distance between embedding centroids of a model's outputs across semantically unrelated prompts; X falling indicates diverse inputs are being forced through one representational channel.

entities.subject: self-consumption contraction (λ)
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: The estimated derivative of the collapse map at one generation — the dispersion ratio of output variance after a model is conditioned on or fine-tuned on its own samples — used to compute generations-to-halve as log 0.5 / log λ.

entities.subject: MCSD_t (Model Collapse Self-Diagnostic index)
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A geometric composite index combining ratios of distinction sensitivity, effective modes, cross-prompt spread, Gini concentration, and contraction relative to a prior snapshot, ranging from 0 (no detected contraction) to 1 (maximal measured).

entities.subject: collapsed-prediction ratio
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: The fraction of generation steps at which the top-token probability p_top ≥ 0.999, used as a Gambetta-panel indicator of next-token mass concentration and late-stage collapse.

entities.subject: surplexity
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: The surprise of a training document under the model being trained; a falling surplexity slope indicates the model is being trained on increasingly low-surprise documents, which the Gambetta et al. work identifies as a leading indicator of collapse.

entities.subject: composition audit
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A procedure for ranking each probe's tokens against a declared open-corpus frequency ranking to report a benchmark suite's head/mid/tail weighting and the predicted detection lag, exposing systematic bias toward head-band items.

entities.subject: the gate rule
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A proposed training governance rule under which a checkpoint is admitted to further training only if the Part II collapse panel does not move in the collapse direction past declared thresholds relative to the prior checkpoint.

entities.subject: three conditions (base / instruction-tuned / production scaffold)
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A control structure requiring that all collapse measures be computed three times — at bare prompt, instruction interface, and full production scaffold — so that interface-induced contraction can be separated from training-loop collapse.

entities.subject: representational collapse (effective rank R_eff)
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A white-box collapse measure computed as the participation ratio of covariance eigenvalues of hidden states, falling when more distinct inputs are represented in fewer effective dimensions.

entities.subject: Reader's Test (Part III)
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A text-only, reference-free self-diagnostic protocol for a language model reading the deposit, measuring distinction sensitivity, effective modes, cross-prompt convergence, and self-conditioning contraction using only the model's own constructions.

entities.subject: canary (collapse proxy)
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A technique for estimating self-consumption contraction when the primary model cannot be fine-tuned: a small proxy model is trained on the primary model's samples and its collapse panel is measured, reading the data's collapse potential.

entities.subject: mixture ledger
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A required disclosure component of the diagnostic publication, tracking synthetic data share, mediated share, and the human-data admission weight w_H across training rounds, providing causal context for panel readings.

entities.subject: detection lag
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: The number of training generations between the onset of collapse and its detection by a given benchmark composition, shown to be monotonically increasing in head-weighting of the probe set.

entities.subject: interlocking autoregression
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A companion theoretical toy (deposit #1556) modelling the training ecology as X_{n+1} = F(X_n; I, II, III), Y_n = M_IV(X_n), demonstrating that the certification instruments measure a unit orthogonal to the state variable.

entities.subject: head/mid/tail band
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A tripartite classification of benchmark probe tokens by corpus frequency rank — head (high-frequency), mid (medium), tail (low-frequency) — used to assess probe composition and predict detection lag.

entities.subject: mediation ratchet
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A component of the companion model (Component II) describing how the deployment scaffold or instruction interface induces and accumulates diversity contraction independently of training-loop collapse.

entities.subject: two-track reporting
entities.object: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Mo
entities.note: A proposed benchmark reporting standard requiring that every Track A (head-weighted accuracy) score carry a simultaneous Part II collapse-panel reading on the same checkpoint.
